subject: FinFlux security milemarkers & retention decisions — MAP kickoff
messages:
From: Elaine Brooks <elaine.brooks@finflux.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, tom.rivera@finflux.com
Date: 2026-11-25T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: FinFlux MAP: security checkpoints and retention windows

Hi Kimberly + Tom,

Thanks for the demo last week — FinFlux is aligned to move forward but we need to lock the security/compliance lane in the MAP before we can commit to a pilot. High level asks from our side:

- Latest SOC 2 Type II report and a short summary of any control exceptions in the past 12 months.
- SIG/CAIQ answers or a short gap doc we can review.
- DPA redline — our legal team will push back around data retention windows and subprocessors.
- Confirmation of data residency options (US/EU) and log retention (audit log TTL).

I attached a first pass at our internal MAP (FinFlux_MAP_v1.xlsx) — it has target dates but we’d like to sync on realistic milestones and owners. We’re targeting a commercial pilot start in mid-December; if security gating drags past 2026-12-15 we may need to delay.

Can we get a proposed MAP and an evidence intake cadence by end of day Tuesday? Also, if Redwood has a standard DPA redline you prefer, please send that.

Thanks,
Elaine Brooks
Head of IT Risk — FinFlux Inc
elaine.brooks@finflux.com
(415) 555-0132

Attachment: FinFlux_MAP_v1.xlsx

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Brooks <elaine.brooks@finflux.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-25T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: FinFlux MAP: security checkpoints and retention windows

Hi Elaine — thanks for the clear asks and the MAP draft. We can absolutely get a tighter security lane in place. Quick readout and proposal:

What Redwood can provide this week:
- SOC 2 Type II report (2026-08-01) + a short three-line summary of controls status.
- SIG/CAIQ answers (we’ll send the self-assessment PDF).
- Standard Redwood DPA redline for your review and a DocuSign-ready copy if legal prefers.
- Proposed evidence intake cadence: weekly 30-minute intake calls, with a shared checklist and a Drive folder for artifacts.

Proposed MAP milestones (draft):
1) Evidence intake kickoff — 2026-12-01 — owners: Kimberly (Redwood) / Elaine (FinFlux)
2) SOC/SIG evidence collection — 2026-12-03 to 2026-12-09 — owners: Security Eng + FinFlux IT
3) DPA redline resolution & signatures — target 2026-12-13
4) Pilot start — 2026-12-15 (contingent on gating)

Decision questions where we need FinFlux input:
- Preferred retention windows for user-level data (options: 90 / 180 / 365 days).
- Any required subprocessor disclosure or additional audit rights beyond standard DPA language.

I attached the Redwood SIG self assessment (Redwood_SIG_self_assessment_v2.pdf) and a short MAP kickoff checklist. Jonas — can you add a brief SOC2 summary and flag any known exceptions in the next message? Karthik — I’ll need a one-pager on acceptance criteria we can put in the MAP.

I’ll upload the DPA redline to DocuSign this afternoon for an initial look. If FinFlux has legal redline preferences, send them back to me and we’ll triage.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Compliance Partnerships | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

Attachments: Redwood_SIG_self_assessment_v2.pdf; MAP_kickoff_checklist.docx

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-25T13:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: FinFlux MAP: security checkpoints and retention windows

Kimberly — quick SOC 2 / gap summary below for the MAP. Internal only.

SOC 2 status (summary):
- Report: SOC 2 Type II, period ending 2026-08-01. No material exceptions; two control findings (minor) around change ticket SLAs — mitigations in place, detail available on request.
- Evidence posture: most artifacts (control docs, config screenshots, policy excerpts) are available. Can stage into Drive folder for FinFlux.

SIG/CAIQ: completed self-assessment available — will share the completed PDF with FinFlux.

DPA / retention options:
- Standard Redwood approach: user-level data retention 90 days by default; operational/audit logs retained 180 days; backups 365 days (encrypted).
- If FinFlux requires alternate windows, propose we model in the MAP as an ask with a signoff decision (change only if legal provides a written exception).

Known blockers / acceleration levers:
- Blocker: FinFlux legal wanting subprocessor-level invoices for 3rd party infra providers may slow signoff.
- Lever: Offer a limited subprocessors disclosure + SOC reports from cloud partners and an on-call security walkthrough.

I’m attaching a very short summary file we’ll include in the Drive.

Jonas
Security Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachment: SOC2_2026-08-01_summary.txt

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Brooks <elaine.brooks@finflux.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-26T09:10:00-08:00
Subject: Re: FinFlux MAP: security checkpoints and retention windows

Hi Elaine — looping in a proposed mutual action plan with acceptance criteria for the security lane. See bullets below (I’ve tried to keep the timeline tight to meet your mid-December pilot ask).

MAP (security lane) — proposed milestones and owners:
- 2026-12-01: Kickoff / evidence intake (30m) — Kimberly (Redwood) / Elaine (FinFlux) — deliverables: Drive folder + access, initial checklist status
- 2026-12-03: SOC/SIG artifact drop — Redwood uploads artifacts; FinFlux confirms review
- 2026-12-07: Technical acceptance run (security tests) — Redwood-run smoke tests against sandbox; FinFlux provides sample payloads/data profile
- 2026-12-10: DPA redline finalization — legal teams reconcile; target signoffs by 2026-12-13
- 2026-12-15: Pilot start (conditional)

Security acceptance checklist (example criteria):
- SOC 2 Type II report provided and no open critical findings
- SIG/CAIQ responses received and major gaps documented with remediation owners
- DPA agreed (retention windows and subprocessors disclosed)
- Sandbox smoke tests pass basic data-flow and residency checks

Evaluation plan notes (short):
- Tests to run during evaluation: residency verification, assertion of token-level logging, KV cache isolation checks for multi-tenant workloads, and a 1-hour latency smoke test at 95th percentile.
- Metrics: 95p latency, token cost per 1k, evidence of KV cache TTL and purge behavior.

Drive doc (proposal): https://drive.google.com/finflux/Redwood-FinFlux-MAP-2026 — I put a draft MAP in the folder (named: Redwood-FinFlux-MAP-draft). Please add your legal redline preference as comments in the Drive doc so we can resolve quickly.

If FinFlux confirms the kickoff date (2026-12-01) we’ll schedule the intake and reserve engineering time for the sandbox run on 2026-12-07.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Sr. Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Brooks <elaine.brooks@finflux.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-27T10:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: FinFlux MAP: security checkpoints and retention windows — agreed draft

Elaine — thanks for the quick review. Per internal triage + Karthik/Jonas input, here’s the agreed draft MAP we’ll operate from unless FinFlux requests changes by 2026-12-03 EOD:

Finalized items (draft):
- Kickoff: 2026-12-01 (intake call + Drive access)
- Evidence window: 2026-12-03 to 2026-12-09
- Acceptance run: 2026-12-07 (sandbox)
- DPA redline delivered to FinFlux: 2026-11-27 (DocuSign link below) — please return any legal comments as inline redlines in the DocuSign packet or via the Drive doc comments.
- Target sign: 2026-12-13
- Pilot start (target): 2026-12-15

Retention proposals (we recommend these defaults to speed approval):
- User-level data: 90 days (configurable on request)
- Operational/audit logs: 180 days
- Backups / cold archives: 365 days (encrypted)

If FinFlux prefers 180 days for user-level data instead of 90 we can accommodate but it will require a brief security review and a signed exception in the MAP.

DocuSign (DPA redline): https://app.docusign.com/share/DPA-Redwood-FinFlux-2026
Drive MAP draft: https://drive.google.com/finflux/Redwood-FinFlux-MAP-2026

Next steps:
1) Elaine to confirm acceptance of kickoff date (2026-12-01) and retention defaults or propose alternate windows by 2026-12-03.
2) If accepted, we’ll schedule the intake and Karthik will book the sandbox run.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this over the line.

Kimberly Park
Head of Compliance Partnerships | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

Attachments: MAP_kickoff_checklist.docx

From: Elaine Brooks <elaine.brooks@finflux.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@finflux.com>
Date: 2026-11-27T16:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: FinFlux MAP: security checkpoints and retention windows — agreed draft

Kimberly / team — that timeline works for us and we’ll aim to keep the target 2026-12-15 pilot. A couple quick notes:

- FinFlux legal will review the DPA redline today and we’ll surface any high-priority comments in the Drive doc.
- We are fine with the default retention windows (90 / 180 / 365) for now. If our privacy team requests a longer user retention window we’ll flag it as an exception in the MAP.
- Please put Dec 1 morning (09:30 PT) as the kickoff slot and send the calendar invite.

I attached a short internal privacy note for context.

Thanks,
Elaine Brooks
Head of IT Risk — FinFlux Inc

Attachment: FinFlux_internal_privacy_note.pdf
